prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Conservative Party Manifesto 2010 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core vision: Shift from “big government” to the “Big Society” by devolving power to individuals, families, professionals and local communities; restore responsibility in public finances; back enterprise and aspiration; and rebuild trust in politics. Guiding belief: “We’re all in this together.”

Economy and public finances
- Eliminate most of the structural deficit over a Parliament via an emergency Budget, £6bn immediate waste cuts, an Office for Budget Responsibility, a 1‑year public sector pay freeze (excluding the lowest paid), and reduced quangos/Whitehall costs.
- Cancel the most damaging parts of Labour’s planned National Insurance rise; cut and simplify business taxes (corporation tax towards 25%, small companies 20%) and set a 5‑year corporate tax roadmap; create an Office of Tax Simplification.
- Rebalance the economy toward saving, investment, exports and hi‑tech/low‑carbon growth; refocus R&D credits, strengthen STEM, improve trade support, superfast broadband rollout, planning reform, and SME access to procurement.
- Welfare-to-work: replace schemes with a single, payment‑by‑results Work Programme; reassess Incapacity Benefit; require community work for the long‑term unemployed who refuse offers.
- Banking reform: Bank of England to lead prudential supervision; safer leverage/funding; a bank levy; more competition; credit access for SMEs.

Society and public services
- Family-friendly UK: recognise marriage/civil partnerships in the tax system; end the couple penalty in tax credits; extend flexible working; flexible parental leave; protect pensioner benefits and re-link state pension to earnings.
- NHS: real-terms funding rises; more patient choice; GP‑led commissioning; scrap non‑clinical targets; publish outcomes; 24/7 urgent care access; Cancer Drugs Fund; integrate health and social care budgets for long‑term conditions.
- Schools: higher standards and discipline; strengthen teacher quality; rigorous curriculum/phonics; reform exams; expand academies/free schools; pupil premium for disadvantaged children; protect special schools; technical academies and apprenticeships.
- Crime and policing: tougher stance on knives; overhaul licensing to curb alcohol-fuelled disorder; elected police commissioners; cut police paperwork; payment‑by‑results rehabilitation; border police force.
- Immigration: annual cap on non‑EU economic migrants; student visa tightening; English test for spouses; transitional EU controls as standard.

Environment and energy
- Lead a low‑carbon economy: cut emissions 80% by 2050; Green Investment Bank; carbon price floor; support nuclear (no subsidy), CCS demos, offshore wind/grid, district heating, and small‑scale generation; Green Deal (home efficiency financed via bill savings).
- Protect nature: stronger biodiversity/habitat protection, fisheries reform, more tree planting; high animal welfare; combat bTB with science‑led badger control; honest food labelling; supermarket ombudsman; move toward a zero‑waste society, water reform, flood resilience.

Politics and localism
- Clean up politics: recall MPs, expenses transparency, cut MPs by ~10%, cut ministers’ pay, curb lobbying abuses, donation cap by agreement.
- Transparency: publish spending, contracts, senior pay/expenses; rein in quangos; overhaul procurement.
- Local power: “open source” planning; neighbourhood planning/control and community rights to run/buy services; local referendums; elected mayors in big cities; protect green belt; help first‑time buyers (stamp duty threshold).
- Civil liberties: scrap ID cards/identity register; reform DNA retention and vetting; UK Bill of Rights.

Foreign, defence and development
- National Security Council; Strategic Defence and Security Review; support mission in Afghanistan; renew Trident; fix procurement; restore the Military Covenant (pay, equipment, family support).
- Foreign policy: liberal Conservative—human rights, strong NATO/US ties, deeper links with India/others; prevent Iranian nuclear weapon; two‑state solution in MEPP.
- Europe: positive engagement, no Euro, “referendum lock” on any future power transfer; seek repatriation of certain powers.
- International development: legislate to reach 0.7% of GNI by 2013; rigorous transparency and results; at least £500m/year to fight malaria; focus on basic services and wealth‑creation institutions; push for pro‑poor trade.
</text>
